events.title: A rowing club
events.text: Clerks and Portuguese merchants found Vasco in Rio on 21 August, named for the 400th anniversary of da Gama's route to India.

events.title: Football begins
events.text: After absorbing Lusitânia Sport Club's football team, Vasco enters competition.

events.title: Promoted
events.text: Vasco win Rio's second tier; Flamengo, Fluminense, Botafogo and América try and fail to block their entry.

events.title: The Camisas Negras
events.text: Trailing 2-0 at General Severiano, Vasco beat São Cristóvão 3-2 on 12 August and clinch the Carioca in their first top-flight season.

events.title: The letter
events.text: On 7 April, president José Augusto Prestes refuses to drop twelve players and withdraws Vasco's application to the new AMEA league.

events.title: Unbeaten elsewhere
events.text: Staying in the LMDT, Vasco win that title with fourteen wins from fourteen.

events.title: Let in
events.text: The AMEA admits Vasco.

events.title: São Januário opens
events.text: On 21 April, with President Washington Luís present, Santos win the opening match, reported as 5-3. Supporters' money built the ground.

events.title: Casaca in print
events.text: The first written record of the shout appears in the newspaper Crítica in October.

events.title: The Victory Express
events.text: The first of five Carioca titles in eight seasons: 1945, 1947, 1949, 1950 and 1952.

events.title: Santiago
events.text: Seven clubs meet for the South American Championship of Champions. Vasco open by beating Bolivia's Litoral 2-1.

events.title: Champions of champions
events.text: River Plate 0-0 Vasco on 14 March clinches the title: unbeaten, 12 goals for and 3 against.

events.title: Arsenal at São Januário
events.text: On 25 May, Vasco beat England's Arsenal 1-0.

events.title: First Maracanã champions
events.text: Vasco win the first Carioca of the Maracanã era; Ademir scores 25 goals in it.

events.title: Seven-one
events.text: On 9 July, Brazil beat Sweden 7-1 at the Maracanã: four for Ademir, two for Chico, one for Maneca, all Vasco men.

events.title: Barbosa
events.text: Brazil lose the final on 16 July. Barbosa, a Black goalkeeper and champion of South America, is unfairly blamed for decades.

events.title: Fifth Express title
events.text: The last Carioca of the Victory Express.

events.title: Bellini's year
events.text: Vasco win the Carioca in the year their captain Bellini first lifts the World Cup for Brazil, in Stockholm.

events.title: Dinamite arrives
events.text: A debut goal for a teenage Roberto against Internacional at the Maracanã on 25 November.

events.title: First national title
events.text: 2-1 v Cruzeiro at the Maracanã on 1 August, in a play-off after finishing level.

events.title: Mazarópi's wall
events.text: From May, the goalkeeper begins a run of more than 1,800 minutes without conceding in the state championship.

events.title: All five
events.text: Back from Barcelona, Roberto Dinamite scores all five in Vasco 5-2 Corinthians on 4 May, before 107,474 at the Maracanã.

events.title: Second title
events.text: Sorato's goal beats São Paulo 1-0 at the Morumbi on 16 December.

events.title: 1948 recognised
events.text: CONMEBOL, based in Paraguay, recognises the 1948 tournament as the precursor of the Libertadores. It is not an official CONMEBOL title.

events.title: Six for Edmundo
events.text: On 11 September, Vasco 6-0 União São João at São Januário: all six by Edmundo, who also misses a penalty.

events.title: Third title
events.text: 0-0 v Palmeiras at the Maracanã on 21 December, after 0-0 in the first leg. Vasco's better earlier record decides it.

events.title: The Monumental
events.text: On 22 July, Juninho Pernambucano's late free kick makes it River Plate 1-1 Vasco, and Vasco go through 2-1 on aggregate.

events.title: Libertadores, first leg
events.text: 2-0 v Barcelona SC at São Januário on 12 August.

events.title: Centenary champions
events.text: 2-1 in Guayaquil on 26 August: Copa Libertadores champions, five days after the club's 100th birthday.

events.title: A world final
events.text: Vasco lose the FIFA Club World Championship final to Corinthians on penalties at the Maracanã on 14 January.

events.title: Peñarol, Montevideo
events.text: The Mercosur road starts with a 4-3 defeat at Peñarol on 1 August.

events.title: San Lorenzo
events.text: San Lorenzo 0-2 Vasco in Buenos Aires on 28 September, in the Mercosur group stage.

events.title: Four at River
events.text: River Plate 1-4 Vasco on 22 November, in the Mercosur semi-final first leg.

events.title: Virada do Século
events.text: On 20 December, 3-0 down at half-time with ten men from the 77th minute, Vasco win the Mercosur decider 4-3 at Palmeiras. Romário scores the 93rd-minute winner.

events.title: The fence collapses
events.text: On 30 December, the São Januário leg of the national final is abandoned at 27 minutes after a crowd crush and fence collapse.

events.title: Fourth title
events.text: The Copa João Havelange is decided on 18 January at the Maracanã: 3-1 v São Caetano, 4-2 on aggregate.

events.title: Goal 1000
events.text: On 20 May at São Januário, a penalty against Sport is Romário's thousandth goal by his own count; other counts are lower.

events.title: First relegation
events.text: Vasco go down for the first time; further relegations follow in 2013, 2015 and 2020.

events.title: Straight back
events.text: Série B champions.

events.title: Copa do Brasil
events.text: Champions on away goals on 8 June, after 1-0 at São Januário and 2-3 at Coritiba.

events.title: Back again
events.text: Promotion sealed on the last day of Série B: Ituano 0-1 Vasco, Nenê's goal.

events.title: A night at Boca
events.text: On 13 October 2026, Adson's goal wins a Sudamericana semi-final first leg at Boca Juniors; Vasco go out 2-3 on aggregate on 20 October.

events.title: A hundred years due
events.text: As of November 2026: São Januário's centenary falls on 21 April 2027, when a time capsule is due to be opened.

chartNote: Share of the area of South America, by today's country boundaries. A simplification: it follows only the three continental title campaigns of 1948, 1998 and 2000, and a country is marked by the clubs Vasco met from it, even when the match was played elsewhere (all of 1948 was played in Santiago). The 1948 tournament is recognised by CONMEBOL as the Libertadores' precursor, not as an official CONMEBOL title.
